title: Protocol and Vector
premise: Casper Kavanagh, a xenolinguist exiled to maintain an orphaned beacon at the edge of settled space, discovers the nine-second gravity flicker was not an accident but a handshake — a signal from something in dead space that has been listening through her beacon for years. As she races toward the relay with the reactor countdown ticking, she learns the system's ruling Consortium built the beacon as a trap and plans to let her die sealing it. In the end Casper chooses to answer the signal herself, broadcasting the truth of the Consortium's crimes in a language no human can censor, and steps into the dark knowing she will never dream in human words again.
about_author: P. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space arrays before turning to fiction. They write from a converted observatory on the coast, where they insist the static still talks back.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Isolated at Beacon Station Kestrel, Casper catalogs languages she no longer dreams in while maintaining equipment nobody claims ownership of. When gravity flickers for nine seconds across the whole system, her instruments record a structured pattern buried inside it — addressed, impossibly, in her own early translation work. The beat: dread curdling into recognition that she has been chosen, or marked.

chapters.title: The Commission Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Casper and relay technician Idris Vane. Digging through sealed records, Casper finds the beacon's true commission: a Consortium black project to bait contact and destroy it. Idris, at the edge relay, receives orders to lock down all traffic — including hers. The beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve as two strangers realize they are being aimed at each other.

chapters.title: Dead Space Countdown
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Casper burns for the relay as Kestrel's reactor begins its rigged countdown; Idris must choose between his orders and her evidence. Consortium interceptors close in, and the signal from dead space grows clearer — patient, ancient, asking a question only Casper can parse. The beat: desperate momentum, trust forged under fire, the climax breaking as Casper reaches the relay seconds before lockdown.

chapters.title: Answering in a Dead Language
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with Idris present. Cornered in the relay, Casper uses its transmitter to broadcast the Consortium's crimes woven into her reply to the signal — justice outside any court, in a language power cannot read or erase. The reactor dies; the flicker returns, gentler now, taking her answer into the dark. The beat: grief transmuted into purpose, as Casper accepts exile among the listeners and Idris carries her testimony home.
